concept: Rush Battlecruiser tech with a compact opening, start the first Battlecruiser before normal economic expansion, then transition into sustained Battlecruiser-led pressure while scaling economy and production.
rules: Keep Battlecruisers as the core army and Marines as support, developing toward roughly 80% Battlecruisers and 20% Marines.
Prioritize Battlecruiser tech and sustained Battlecruiser production over nonessential spending.
Preserve Battlecruisers and avoid unnecessary losses or unfavorable trades.
After the first Battlecruiser enters production, expand one base at a time and do not exceed four total bases.

enter_when: The Fusion Core and Starport Tech Lab are not both ready.
This usually occurs within approximately 0-4 minutes; time is only a weak reference.
phases.goal: Complete the tech path required for the first Battlecruiser as quickly as possible.
guidance: Prioritize the fixed Battlecruiser opening over expansion, extra production, unrelated tech, or nonessential units.
At 12 supply, build one Supply Depot, one Refinery, and one Barracks, then train three SCVs.
At 15 supply, start one Factory, train one Marine, upgrade the Command Center to an Orbital Command, build the second Refinery, then train one Marine and two SCVs.
At 17 supply, start one Starport, then train one Marine, two SCVs, and one more Marine.
At 19 supply, build one Supply Depot, one Fusion Core, and a Tech Lab on the Starport.
Keep early Marines near the main base for defense.
Avoid spending that significantly delays the Starport, Fusion Core, or Starport Tech Lab.
Keep the opening close to the planned scale: roughly 4 Marines, 2 Refineries, and one each of Barracks, Factory, Starport, Fusion Core, and Starport Tech Lab.
Finish this phase when both the Fusion Core and Starport Tech Lab are ready.

enter_when: The Fusion Core and Starport Tech Lab are ready, but no Battlecruiser is ready or in production.
phases.goal: Start the first Battlecruiser as soon as possible.
guidance: Reserve 400 minerals, 300 vespene, and 6 supply for the first Battlecruiser.
Avoid expansion, extra production, upgrades, or nonessential units if they would delay the first Battlecruiser.
Keep Marines near the main base for defense.
Start the first Battlecruiser as soon as resources and supply are available.
Finish this phase once a Battlecruiser enters production.

enter_when: The first Battlecruiser is in production, but no Battlecruiser is ready yet.
This usually occurs around approximately 4-6 minutes; time is only a weak reference.
phases.goal: Use the first Battlecruiser's production window to begin economic and production growth without disrupting Battlecruiser production.
guidance: Keep the first Battlecruiser in production and prioritize continued Battlecruiser production.
Begin normal macro growth: add SCVs, supply, Refineries, production capacity, and take the natural as the second base as resources allow.
Expansion is now allowed one base at a time, but should not significantly delay continued Battlecruiser production.
Develop toward roughly 80% Battlecruisers and 20% Marines.
Keep Marines near the main base for defense until the first Battlecruiser is ready.
Finish this phase as soon as the first Battlecruiser is ready.

enter_when: At least one Battlecruiser is ready.
This usually occurs after approximately 5-6 minutes; time is only a weak reference.
phases.goal: Apply continuous Battlecruiser-led pressure while scaling economy, production, and army strength.
guidance: Start pressure as soon as the first Battlecruiser is ready rather than waiting for a large army.
Keep Battlecruisers as the main force and Marines as support, developing toward roughly 80% Battlecruisers and 20% Marines.
Continue Battlecruiser production while adding SCVs, Refineries, supply, production capacity, and expansions up to four total bases as resources allow.
Move Marines from main-base defense into offensive support after the first Battlecruiser is ready.
Prioritize significant enemy army concentrations when they present a useful engagement; otherwise pressure known enemy structures.
If no useful enemy target is known, pressure the enemy starting area, then search likely expansion locations.
Avoid concentrated anti-air threats and unsafe routes when possible.
Use Tactical Jump for long-distance engagement or repositioning, preferably to a safe position near the attack target.
Retreat badly damaged Battlecruisers, especially below roughly 225 health, rather than losing them unnecessarily.
Prioritize sustained Battlecruiser production over excessive expansion or Marine production.
